page: The Vultr vhp-4c-8gb-intel is a High Performance series instance powered by an Intel Xeon processor on the x86_64 architecture. It provides 4 shared virtual CPUs derived from 2 physical cores with hyperthreading enabled at a base frequency of 2.0 GHz. Memory capacity is provisioned at 8.0 GB, establishing a 1:2 vCPU-to-RAM ratio (2.0 GB per core). CPU cache layout comprises 32 KB L1 data cache, 4 MB L2 cache, and 16 MB shared L3 cache. Storage is bundled directly into the profile via a 180 GB local NVMe SSD. The instance contains no dedicated GPUs and includes one complimentary public IPv4 address.

Benchmark evaluation reveals mid-range single-core capability paired with entry-level multi-core and memory subsystem throughput under load. Single-core stress-ng tests reached 1,456.98, and Geekbench single-core scored 1,182.0, both placing within median industry percentiles. In contrast, multi-threaded metrics such as stress-ng multi-core (5,760.92) and Geekbench multi-core (3,820.0) placed in lower performance tiers. The memory architecture sustained 409.04 GB/sec on small cached 16 KB read blocks, but uncached 256 MB reads dropped to 36.98 GB/sec. The instance managed 6.27 million operations per second in Redis SET evaluations, while static web serving throughput reached 6.27 GB/sec.

From an efficiency standpoint, the vhp-4c-8gb-intel combines modern vector instruction sets—such as AVX-512 and AVX-512 VNNI—with fast local NVMe storage at a lightweight hardware footprint. Because CPU resources are allocated on a shared basis, multi-tenant contention can impact sustained compute jobs such as compilation, physics calculations, or heavy parallel decompression. This configuration is best suited for workloads requiring fast local disk input/output and modest memory density, including staging environments, continuous integration agents, lightweight microservices, caching layers, and intermediate web application hosting.
description: The Vultr vhp-4c-8gb-intel is a virtual server instance configured with 4 shared vCPUs derived from 2 physical Intel Xeon cores operating at 2.0 GHz on the x86_64 architecture. The platform includes 8.0 GB of system memory, matching a 1:2 compute-to-memory ratio, alongside 180 GB of integrated local NVMe SSD storage. L3 cache is sized at 16 MB, with hardware instruction support for AVX-512 and AES cryptography. Synthetic benchmarks show average single-thread compute capabilities alongside modest multi-core throughput, reflected in stress-ng and Geekbench multi-core tiers. The server records in-memory Redis throughput of 6.27 million operations per second, though large-block memory transfers and static web serving yield lower performance tiers due to shared resource allocation. This instance delivers a cost-efficient profile for moderate batch tasks, staging environments, microservices, and lightweight web serving where dedicated core isolation is not required.
